title: the day-0 oracle: falsifiable predictions registered BEFORE the dump
note: every prediction is derived from persisted registers only (zero downloads, zero hardware) and carries its own falsifier. The dump of 16/09 and the next vendor release become EXAMS with expected answers, scored mechanically by fw35-oracle.py score. A prediction is never edited after registration; a wrong prediction is scored miss and the cause is written in the next ring report. Bands are anchored on the target board's own measured values, never on corpus-wide ranges (the ASUS varstore share is 83.89%, below the 84-90% corpus band — corpus ranges must not be transplanted onto single boards).

targets.day0-3644: the physical board dump on 16/09 (ASUS B450-PLUS class, reports BIOS 3644) — resolves question_3644 (vendor-ledger-tuf.json H3)
targets.release-41: the next PRIME B450-PLUS release after 4655, whenever it lands — scored from the same ring-16 probe machinery on the new CAP

verdicts.hit: observed inside the registered band / equal to the registered value / predicate true
verdicts.partial: observed inside the widened band but outside the registered one — direction right, magnitude off
verdicts.miss: outside both — the register is falsified on this point
verdicts.na: the predicate's precondition did not hold (only registered predicates can be na)

scoring.protocol: score computed ONLY by lab/fw35-oracle.py score <findings.json>; the findings file maps prediction id to the observed value(s) named in each prediction's 'observed_key'; every partial and miss requires a written cause in the following ring report; the register file is frozen after commit

predictions.claim: the dump is a 16 MiB part: 16,777,216 bytes exactly
basis: vendor-flash-armor.json probes: rom_bytes=16777216 at all nine rungs 3604-4655
predictions.falsifier: any other size (32 MiB part would falsify the board-class assumption itself)

predictions.claim: the ComboAM4v2PI level sits in the closed set {1.2.0.6b, 1.2.0.6c, 1.2.0.7}; single-point guess 1.2.0.6c (3644 dates between 3604=1.2.0.6b 2022/03/16 and 3802=1.2.0.7 2022/05/12)
basis: vendor-agesa.json: nine-point byte-verified chronology brackets 3644 between 1.2.0.6b and 1.2.0.7
vendor-ledger-tuf.json question_3644: H3 open, the dump decides
predictions.falsifier: any level outside the widened set (e.g. 1.2.0.A) — would break the dated bracket and reopen the identity question wider than H3

predictions.claim: the AGESA version string carries the ComboAM4v2PI prefix (B450 is AM4; 9/9 rungs carry it)
basis: vendor-agesa.json first_hits: 'ComboAM4v2PI <level>' at every rung of the nine-point chronology
predictions.falsifier: any other prefix (ComboAM4v1 would falsify the board-generation assumption; ComboAM5 would falsify the socket)

predictions.claim: the core armor quartet is ABSENT (3644 precedes the 3802 wave-1 boundary; last_without=3604)
basis: vendor-flash-armor.json wave1_boundary: first_with_core=3802, last_without=3604; probes[3604].core_armor=0, added_present=[]
predictions.falsifier: quartet present — would contradict the wave-1 boundary measured at probe granularity and demand a re-derivation of the bisect

predictions.claim: the SbRomArmorSmm module is ABSENT (born 3802, one byte-identical body since)
basis: vendor-genome.json wave1_births: 5 species born exactly at 3802
docs/day0-report-2026-09-16.md section 1.5: SbRomArmorSmm byte-identical since 3802
predictions.falsifier: module present at 3644 — births-before-wave would falsify the genome birth law

predictions.claim: the SPI chip whitelist carries the 41-family predecessor set (the 46-family armor set expands only at 3802) and no 'AMD rom armor' banner
basis: vendor-armor-chipdb.json ladder_movement: 3604->3802 is the only expansion, 41->46, +5 (Cypress 25FS-S, Fudan FM25W, MXIC 77L, XMC 25RH, XMC 25RU); the whitelist belongs to the AMI flash driver and predates the armor
predictions.falsifier: 46 families or the armor banner at 3644 — the whitelist would have moved without the armor, contradicting the single-expansion ladder

predictions.claim: exactly 2 unnamed legacy SMM modules present (the 3604 removed_present pattern; they die at 4202 and 4402)
basis: vendor-flash-armor.json probes[3604].removed_present: 2x 'SMM (unnamed)'
vendor-genome.json: species deaths EXACTLY the two legacy retirements (4202, 4402)
predictions.falsifier: 0 at 3644 would antedate the retirements; 4+ would antedate the wave births

predictions.claim: total FFS modules in [600, 640]; point guess 618 (the 3604 sentinel count; 3644 is a close neighbor build)
basis: vendor-flash-armor.json probes[3604].modules = 618
vendor-genome.json per_rung_file_counts: rung-to-rung file-count movement is tens, never hundreds, outside rebuild events
predictions.falsifier: outside the widened band — would make 3644 a distant build, not a neighbor (identity consequence feeds P-18)

predictions.claim: the main DSDT body hash is 27d5e826e111d755 (generation 1, held unchanged 3604 through 4202)
basis: vendor-ssdt-clock.json per_specimen: asus-3604/3802/3810/4003/4202 main_dsdt.sha16 = 27d5e826e111d755; generations move only at 4202->4402 and 4604->4631
predictions.falsifier: any other hash — a fourth DSDT generation before 4402 would break the three-generation clock

predictions.claim: the AOD SSDT sits at the pre-armor revision 15 (the rev-153 rewrite is the 3802 armor release)
basis: vendor-ssdt-clock.json ssdt_movement_ladder: 3604->3802 moves one AOD table rev 15->153 (the armor release); the CPM-family wholesale rewrite is 3810->4003
predictions.falsifier: revision 153 at 3644 — the SSDT clock would have moved before the armor it currently dates

predictions.claim: exactly 4 distinct trust certificates (the 3604-3802 band; 6 only from 3810, then the count never changes again)
basis: vendor-der-inventory.json per_specimen: asus-3604 trust_distinct=4, asus-3810 trust_distinct=6; the count never changes after 3810 while bodies rotate
predictions.falsifier: 6 certs at 3644 — the cert expansion would precede 3810; 3 or fewer would contradict the factory baseline

predictions.claim: the setup facade carries 7,900-8,050 questions; point guess 7,975 (the measured 3604-ref value; growth to 8,273 spans thirteen releases)
basis: vendor-ifr-census.json specimens: asus-prime-b450-plus-ref (3604) questions=7,975 / pages=779; asus-prime-b450-plus (4655) questions=8,273 / pages=783
predictions.falsifier: outside the widened band — a facade shrink below 7,700 has no precedent in the chronology

predictions.claim: 100% of form packages valid by exact consumption (every HII package consumed to the last byte)
basis: vendor-ifr-census.json: 100% exact consumption across the six vendor-representative specimens, 46,000+ questions
predictions.falsifier: any invalid package — would be the first in the corpus and would question the ring-6/19 grammar port

predictions.claim: the factory Setup varstore is 456 bytes (+/- 16) — the ring-14 blob ring-20 priced
basis: vendor-unasked.json coverage[asus-prime-b450-plus-ref].setup_row: size=456, covered=314, questions=368
predictions.falsifier: size beyond +/-32 — the factory defaults blob is stable across the chronology; a big delta would signal a defaults rewrite

predictions.claim: 142 never-asked bytes inside the Setup varstore (+/- 16) — the unasked surface the UI cannot reach
basis: vendor-unasked.json coverage[asus-prime-b450-plus-ref].setup_row: uncovered=142 (456-314)
predictions.falsifier: 0 uncovered — the hidden surface would have closed, contradicting the variable-level hiding law

predictions.claim: 83.0-86.0% of varstore bytes never referenced by any question (the ASUS board's own measured share, NOT the 84-90% corpus band)
basis: vendor-unasked.json coverage[asus-prime-b450-plus-ref].uncovered_share_pct = 83.89 (71 varstores, 26,027 bytes)
predictions.falsifier: below 80% — the never-asked share would have collapsed; above 90% would place 3644 outside every measured vendor value

predictions.claim: SMM-class census (SMM + SMM-core) in [106, 109]; point guess 106 (the 3604 value 105+1)
basis: vendor-lifecycles.json smm_anatomy.smm_census_per_rung: 3604 SMM=105+SMM-core=1; 3802-4003 SMM=108+1; 4202 SMM=107+1; 4402 SMM=106+1
docs/day0-report-2026-09-16.md section 1.5: expected 107-109 (register convention)

predictions.claim: question_3644 resolves to H3 (published-but-unlisted / region-split): the dump triangulates to NO release of the 40-release ledger and differs from both neighbors (3604, 3802) by at least 3 independent fingerprints (module count, DSDT/SSDT bodies, PSP table set, NVRAM defaults, IFR totals)
basis: vendor-ledger-tuf.json question_3644: H1 proven for the acquisition (240-byte HTML error page), H2 tested dead on both TUF ledgers, H3 open — the dump decides by fingerprints
predictions.falsifier: the dump matches a known ledger release exactly (H3 dead, H2-class variant instead), or differs from both neighbors by fewer than 3 fingerprints (then 3644 is metadata-only and the board already runs a known build)

predictions.claim: the 3644 PSP body-hash set overlaps 3604's MORE than it overlaps 3802's: |h(3644) ∩ h(3604)| > |h(3644) ∩ h(3802)|
basis: vendor-psp-authorship.json: PSP bodies are per-rung material with rare universal bodies; a close-neighbor build should share more with its predecessor than with the next-wave rung
vendor-agesa.json: 3644 brackets between 3604 and 3802
predictions.falsifier: the reversed inequality — 3644 would be PSP-closer to the armor release than to its chronological predecessor, an identity anomaly to investigate before anything else

predictions.claim: the AGESA level of the next release is >= 1.2.0.12 (never lower; the nine-point chronology is strictly monotone)
basis: vendor-agesa.json: 1.2.0.6b -> 1.2.0.12 monotone across all nine dated rungs
predictions.falsifier: a level below 1.2.0.12 — a downgrade has no precedent in 4.5 years

predictions.claim: no third armor wave in a routine release: core_armor stays 4 and added stays 7 (waves are 2 in 4.5 years; both coincided with named security events)
basis: vendor-flash-armor.json probes: core_armor=4 and added=7 constant from 4604 through 4655
vendor-genome.json: births EXACTLY the two security waves
predictions.falsifier: any added module beyond the 7 — a third wave (which would immediately re-open the causality question ring 18 corrected)

predictions.claim: zero species born and zero dead in a routine release (births/deaths coincide with security waves and legacy retirements only)
basis: vendor-genome.json: 330 species, births exactly the two waves (5 @3802, 2 @4604), deaths exactly the two retirements (4202, 4402)
predictions.falsifier: any birth or death — the genome law extends to a third event class

predictions.claim: the distinct trust certificate count stays 6 (unchanged since 3810 across seven rungs; bodies may rotate — the DigiCert chain re-issues at five frontiers)
basis: vendor-der-inventory.json per_specimen: 6 at every rung 3810-4655; trust_movement_ladder: bodies rotate, count frozen
predictions.falsifier: 7+ would be a new cert class (count never moved); 5 or fewer would be a retirement with no precedent

predictions.claim: the facade never shrinks: questions >= 8,273 (the 4655 value)
basis: vendor-ifr-census.json: ASUS chronology 7,975 (3604) -> 8,273 (4655), growth across the chronology; no measured shrink in the corpus
predictions.falsifier: below 8,273 — the first measured facade shrink (which would itself be a finding worth a ring)

predictions.claim: the DSDT generation moves ONLY if the AGESA level moves: if AGESA stays 1.2.0.12, the DSDT hash stays 0a4a6f162cad3e51 (generations moved only at AGESA-swap rungs 4202->4402 and 4604->4631)
basis: vendor-ssdt-clock.json generations: three bodies across nine rungs, both moves at AGESA-swap transitions
vendor-agesa.json: the same two transitions carry the largest module deltas (churn atlas)
predictions.falsifier: AGESA unchanged AND DSDT changed — the DSDT clock would have decoupled from the AGESA clock (scored miss); AGESA changed AND DSDT changed scores na (the precondition dissolved)

predictions.claim: the SPI chip whitelist stays at 46 families (zero set changes 3802 through 4655, 4.5 years)
basis: vendor-armor-chipdb.json: byte-identical table, zero set changes across all measured rungs since 3802
predictions.falsifier: any change — the frozen whitelist would have moved for the first time since the armor
